newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call closes lower, gilts yield plummets.
newsitem.headline: Indian call closes lower, gilts yield plummets.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed lower at 4.00-4.50 percent on Monday, against the day's opening levels of 5.00-5.50 percent, dealers said
Most of the deals were in the region of 4.50-5.00 percent, they said.

"Call rates are expected to hover in the range of 5.00-7.00 percent till mid-June," a dealer with a private bank said. "The rates are expected to open at 5.0 percent on Tuesday, and may slide further to 4.0 percent by close," he said.
"Rumours of a fresh issue for 6-year maturity government stock for 30.0 billion rupees, affected market sentiment in call and security markets," a state-run bank dealer said.
Securities yields have plummeted across-the-board, dealers said.
Volumes on the National Stock Exchange were steady at 1.65 billion rupees on Monday, Umesh Gupta, a dealer at Mata Securities said.
"The 12.69 percent government stock 2002 rose by 25 basis points to 100.60 rupees, while the 11.64 percent stock rose to 98.70 rupees, against its cum-voucher price of 98.55 rupees," Gupta said.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in April 1998 was unchanged at 9.55 percent, he said.
